description: Import single or multi-volume disk images or EBS snapshots into an Amazon Machine Image (AMI).

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: architecture
parameters.description: The architecture of the virtual machine. Choices: "i386" "x86_64"

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: boot_mode
parameters.description: The boot mode of the virtual machine. Choices: "legacy-bios" "uefi"

parameters.name: cancel_reason
parameters.description: The reason for canceling the task.

parameters.name: client_data
parameters.description: The client-specific data.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: A user-defined comment about the disk upload.

parameters.name: upload_end
parameters.description: The time that the disk upload ends.

parameters.name: upload_size
parameters.description: The size of the uploaded disk image, in GiB.

parameters.name: upload_start
parameters.description: The time that the disk upload starts.

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: A description string for the import image task.

parameters.name: disk_containers
parameters.description: Information about the disk containers.

parameters.name: device_name
parameters.description: The block device mapping for the disk.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The format of the disk image being imported. Choices: "OVA" "ova" "VHD" "vhd" "VHDX" "vhdx" "VMDK" "vmdk" "RAW" "raw"

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: The ID of the EBS snapshot to be used for importing the snapshot.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to the Amazon S3-based disk image being imported. The URL can either be a https URL (https://..) or an Amazon S3 URL (s3://..).

parameters.name: user_bucket
parameters.description: The S3 bucket for the disk image.

parameters.name: s3_bucket
parameters.description: The name of the Amazon S3 bucket where the disk image is located.

parameters.name: s3_key
parameters.description: The file name of the disk image.

parameters.name: encrypted
parameters.description: Specifies whether the destination AMI of the imported image should be encrypted. The default KMS key for EBS is used unless you specify a non-default KMS key using kms_key_id. Choices: false true

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: hypervisor
parameters.description: The target hypervisor platform. Choices: "xen"

parameters.name: kms_key_id
parameters.description: An identifier for the symmetric KMS key to use when creating the encrypted AMI. This parameter is only required if you want to use a non-default KMS key; if this parameter is not specified, the default KMS key for EBS is used. If a kms_key_id is specified, the encrypted flag must also be set.

parameters.name: license_specifications
parameters.description: The ARNs of the license configurations.

parameters.name: license_configuration_arn
parameters.description: The ARN of a license configuration.

parameters.name: license_type
parameters.description: The license type to be used for the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) after importing.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The operating system of the virtual machine. Choices: "Windows" "Linux"

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: role_name
parameters.description: The name of the role to use when not using the default role, ‘vmimport’.

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Use state=present to import single or multi-volume disk images or EBS snapshots into an Amazon Machine Image (AMI). Use state=absent to cancel an in-process import virtual machine task. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: The tags to apply to the import image task during creation.

parameters.name: task_name
parameters.description: The name of the EC2 image import task.

parameters.name: usage_operation
parameters.description: The usage operation value.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

examples:
# Note: These examples do not set authentication details, see the AWS Guide for details.
- name: Import image
  amazon.aws.ec2_import_image:
    state: present
    task_name: "clone-vm-import-image"
    disk_containers:
      - format: raw
        user_bucket:
          s3_bucket: "clone-vm-s3-bucket"
          s3_key: "clone-vm-s3-bucket/ubuntu-vm-clone.raw"

- name: Cancel an import image task
  amazon.aws.ec2_import_image:
    state: absent
    task_name: "clone-vm-import-image"

return_values.name: import_image
return_values.description: A dict containing information about an EC2 import task. Returned: always

return_values.name: architecture
return_values.description: The architecture of the virtual machine. Returned: success

return_values.name: description
return_values.description: A description string for the import image task. Returned: success

return_values.name: encrypted
return_values.description: Specifies whether the destination AMI of the imported image should be encrypted. Returned: success

return_values.name: hypervisor
return_values.description: The target hypervisor platform. Returned: success

return_values.name: image_id
return_values.description: The ID of the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) created by the import task. Returned: success

return_values.name: import_task_id
return_values.description: The task ID of the import image task. Returned: success

return_values.name: kms_key_id
return_values.description: The identifier for the symmetric KMS key that was used to create the encrypted AMI. Returned: success

return_values.name: license_specifications
return_values.description: The ARNs of the license configurations. Returned: success

return_values.name: license_type
return_values.description: The license type to be used for the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) after importing. Returned: success

return_values.name: platform
return_values.description: The operating system of the virtual machine. Returned: success

return_values.name: progress
return_values.description: The progress of the task. Returned: success

return_values.name: role_name
return_values.description: The name of the role to use when not using the default role, ‘vmimport’. Returned: success

return_values.name: snapshot_details
return_values.description: Describes the snapshot created from the imported disk. Returned: success

return_values.name: device_name
return_values.description: The block device mapping for the snapshot. Returned: success

return_values.name: disk_image_size
return_values.description: The size of the disk in the snapshot, in GiB. Returned: success

return_values.name: format
return_values.description: The format of the disk image from which the snapshot is created. Returned: success

return_values.name: snapshot_id
return_values.description: The snapshot ID of the disk being imported. Returned: success

return_values.name: status
return_values.description: A brief status of the snapshot creation. Returned: success

return_values.name: status_message
return_values.description: A detailed status message for the snapshot creation. Returned: success

return_values.name: url
return_values.description: The URL used to access the disk image. Returned: success

return_values.name: user_bucket
return_values.description: The Amazon S3 bucket for the disk image. Returned: success

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: The tags to apply to the import image task during creation. Returned: success

return_values.name: task_name
return_values.description: The name of the EC2 image import task. Returned: success

return_values.name: usage_operation
return_values.description: The usage operation value. Returned: success
